verses.sloka: जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि ।ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करं यथा ॥ २.१००.१॥
verses.transliteration: jaṭilaṁ cīravasanaṁ prāñjaliṁ patitaṁ bhuvi ।dadarśa rāmo durdarśaṁ yugānte bhāskaraṁ yathā ॥ 2.100.1॥

translations.english: Rama beheld Bharata with matted locks and robes of bark fallen down on the ground with folded hands like the Sun at the time of dissolution of the world. It was really difficult to look at him.

verses.sloka: कथञ्चिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम् ।भ्रातरं भरतं राम: परिजग्राह बाहुना ॥ २.१००.२॥
verses.transliteration: kathañcidabhivijñāya vivarṇavadanaṁ kṛśam ।bhrātaraṁ bharataṁ rāma: parijagrāha bāhunā ॥ 2.100.2॥

translations.english: Rama found it extremely difficult to recognise Bharata with his emaciated body and pallid face. He held him in his arms and lifted him.
translations.hindi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी ने सीता से कहा-देखो, यह मांस पवित्र है ओर अभ्नि में भूजने से यह स्वादिष्ट हो गया है श्रीरामचन्द्र जी सीलासहित वहाँ बैठे हुए बातंचीत कर रहे थे कि,

verses.sloka: आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघव: ।अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत् समाहितः ॥ २.१००.३॥
verses.transliteration: āghrāya rāmastaṁ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghava: ।aṅke bharatamāropya paryapṛcchat samāhitaḥ ॥ 2.100.3॥

translations.english: Born in the race of Raghu, Rama embraced Bharata and kissed him on his forehead. Placing him on his lap, he enquired thus with a composed mind:
translations.hindi: इतने में उनके पास आती हुई अरत जी की सेना के चलने से उड़ो हुई आकाश को छती हुई धूल देख पड़ी ओर कोलाहल सुनाई दिआ

verses.sloka: क्व नु ते ऽभूत् पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागत: ।न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि ॥ २.१००.४॥
verses.transliteration: kva nu te 'bhūt pitā tāta yadaraṇyaṁ tvamāgata: ।na hi tvaṁ jīvatastasya vanamāgantumarhasi ॥ 2.100.4॥

translations.english: O dear, now that you have come to the forest, where is our father king Dasaratha? You ought not come to the forest while he is living.
translations.hindi: उस महाकोलाहल से त्रस्त हो, बड़े बड़े यूथपति गजेन्द्र विकल हो अपने अपने यूथों को ले इधर उधर भागने लगे

verses.sloka: चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम् ।दुष्प्रतीकमरण्ये ऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागत: ॥ २.१००.५॥
verses.transliteration: cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrādbharatamāgatam ।duṣpratīkamaraṇye 'smin kiṁ tāta vanamāgata: ॥ 2.100.5॥

translations.english: You have come a long distance (from Ayodhya) to this forest, O Bharata It is a pity, dear brother, to see you after a long time, so emaciated. What brings you to the forest?

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्धारयते तात राजा यत्त्वमिहागत: ।कच्चिन्न दीन: सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गत: ॥ २.१००.६॥
verses.transliteration: kacciddhārayate tāta rājā yattvamihāgata: ।kaccinna dīna: sahasā rājā lokāntaraṁ gata: ॥ 2.100.6॥

translations.english: My dear (brother), now that you have come here, I trust, king Dasaratha is keeping good health and hope, he has not departed prematurely in despondency for the other world.
translations.hindi: उन हाथियों को भागते देख और सेना का कोलाहल सुन श्रीरामचन्द्र जी ने तेजस्वी लक्ष्मण से कहा

verses.sloka: कच्चित् सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम् ॥ २.१००.७॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit saumya na te rājyaṁ bhraṣṭaṁ bālasya śāśvatam ॥ 2.100.7॥

translations.english: O gentle one, being young and inexperienced, I trust, you have not forfeited the kingdom for ever. Dear child, I trust, you are looking after father whose prowess is his truthfulness.
translations.hindi: हे लक्ष्मण ! तुमसे पुत्र को पा कर सुमित्रा देवी सुपुत्रवती है । देखो तो, यह भयङ्कर बादल की गड्गड़ाहट जैसे गम्भीर एवं तुमुल शब्द कहाँ सुन पड़ता दै

verses.sloka: कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितरं सत्यविक्रमम् ॥ २.१००.८॥
verses.transliteration: kaccicchuśrūṣase tāta pitaraṁ satyavikramam ॥ 2.100.8॥

translations.english: I trust king Dasaratha, who is true to his promise, a performer of Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices and a firm adherent of righteousness is in good health.
translations.hindi: जिसको सुन, सघन वनवासी हाथियों के झु ड, जंगली मैंसे ओर मृगों के झु ड सिंहों सहित भयभीत हो बड़ी तेजी से इधर उधर भाग रहे हें

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्दशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसङ्गर: ।राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्त्ता धर्मनिश्चय: ॥ २.१००.९॥
verses.transliteration: kacciddaśaratho rājā kuśalī satyasaṅgara: ।rājasūyāśvamedhānāmāharttā dharmaniścaya: ॥ 2.100.9॥

translations.english: O dear child I trust, the family preceptor of the Ikshvakus, Vasistha, the brahmin (versed in the Vedas), who is learned, ever fixed in virtues and effulgent is being honoured as usual.

verses.sloka: स कच्चिद् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युति: ।इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते ॥ २.१००.१०॥
verses.transliteration: sa kaccid brāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyuti: ।ikṣvākūṇāmupādhyāyo yathāvattāta pūjyate ॥ 2.100.10॥

translations.english: Dear child I trust, Kausalya and Sumitra, mothers of an excellent progeny are happy. I trust, the noble queen Kaikeyi is happy too.
translations.hindi: हे लक्ष्मण ! इस रदद पर अब पक्षी भी तो भली माँति नहीं घूम सकते । अतएव तुम. शीघ्र इस बात का ठीक ठीक पता. लगाओ

verses.sloka: सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती ।सुखिनी कच्चिदार्य्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी ॥ २.१००.११॥
verses.transliteration: sā tāta kaccitkausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī ।sukhinī kaccidāryyā ca devī nandati kaikayī ॥ 2.100.11॥

translations.english: I trust, you continue to honour the family priest (Suyajna, son of Vasistha) who is endowed with modesty, born of high family, conversant in scriptures, free from envy and who can give you directions with regard to your duties.
translations.hindi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी का ऐसा वचन सुन लक्ष्मण जी तुरन्त एक फूले हुए साल बृत्ष पर चढ़ गए और चारों ओर देखते हुए उन्होंने प्रथम पूव दिशा की ओर देखा

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्विनयसम्पन्न: कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुत: ।अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहित: ॥ २.१००.१२॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidvinayasampanna: kulaputro bahuśruta: ।anasūyuranudraṣṭā satkṛtaste purohita: ॥ 2.100.12॥

translations.english: I trust, the sagacious priest who knows ritual precepts, who is upright and is employed to take care of your sacred fires, informs you always regarding what was offered and what is to be offered as oblation at appropriate time.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजु: ।हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा ॥ २.१००.१३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidagniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimānṛju: ।hutaṁ ca hoṣyamāṇaṁ ca kāle vedayate sadā ॥ 2.100.13॥

translations.english: Dear brother, I trust you continue to pay homage to gods, father, mothers, teachers, relations equal to your father, aged people, physicians and brahmins.
translations.hindi: हाथियों घोड़ों से युक्त, रथ की पताकाओं से भूषित, उस सेना का वृत्तान्त निवेदन करते हुए, लद््रण्‌ जी ने श्रीरामचन्द्र जी से कहा

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्देवान् पितऽन् मातऽर्गुरून् पितृसमानपि ।वृद्धांश्च तत वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे ॥ २.१००.१४॥
verses.transliteration: kacciddevān pita'n māta'rgurūn pitṛsamānapi ।vṛddhāṁśca tata vaidyāṁśca brāhmaṇāṁścābhimanyase ॥ 2.100.14॥

translations.english: I hope you treat with respect Sudhanva who is equipped with the most formidable arrows and other weapons propelled by mantras and a master in the science of statecraft.
translations.hindi: यह्‌ सुन पुरुषसिह्‌ श्रोरामचन्द्र जो ने लक्ष्मण जी से कहा, हे वत्स सौमित्र ! ध्वज चिह्णों को देख यह वो निश्चय करो कि यह सेना है किसकी ?

verses.sloka: इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्रविशारदम् ।सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे ॥ २.१००.१५॥
verses.transliteration: iṣvastravarasampannamarthaśāstraviśāradam ।sudhanvānamupādhyāyaṁ kaccittvaṁ tāta manyase ॥ 2.100.15॥

translations.english: I hope, dear brother, you have appointed men who are brave, learned, selfcontrolled, of noble birth and skilled in guessing from hints.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदात्मसमा: शूरा: श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रिया: ।कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिण: ॥ २.१००.१६॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidātmasamā: śūrā: śrutavanto jitendriyā: ।kulīnāśceṅgitajñāśca kṛtāste tāta mantriṇa: ॥ 2.100.16॥

translations.english: O Bharata the wellguarded advice of ministers, learned in scriptures and capable of proper counselling, is the root of victory for kings, specially when the advice is kept in confidence.
translations.hindi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी के ऐसे वचन सुन, लक्ष्मण जी क्रोध के : मारे अग्नि के समान हो, उस सेना को मानों भस्म कर डालने के लिए यह बोले,

verses.sloka: मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव ।सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यै: शास्त्रकोविदै: ॥ २.१००.१७॥
verses.transliteration: mantro vijayamūlaṁ hi rājñāṁ bhavati rāghava ।susaṁvṛto mantradharairamātyai: śāstrakovidai: ॥ 2.100.17॥

translations.english: I trust you are not under the grip of sleep but wake up at appropriate times, I hope you always think of the means of judicious statecraft during the last part of the night.
translations.hindi: साफ देख पड़ता है कि, केकेयी का पुत्र भरते राज्याभिषेक पा कर भी, अकण्टक राज्य करने की कामना से, हम दोनों का वध करने के लिए आ रहा है

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषी: कच्चित्काले प्रबुध्यसे ।कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तयस्यर्थनैपुणम् ॥ २.१००.१८॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinnidrāvaśaṁ naiṣī: kaccitkāle prabudhyase ।kacciccāpararātreṣu cintayasyarthanaipuṇam ॥ 2.100.18॥

translations.english: I hope you neither decide alone nor discuss with many. I trust a decision once made by you is not leaked in the kingdom.
translations.hindi: देखिए, वह जो बड़ा और खूब हराभरा सुन्दर बृ देख पड़ता है, उसके पास जो रथ है, उस पर कचनार वृक्ष के आकार की ध्वजा फहरा रही है

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैक: कच्चिन्न बहुभि: सह ।कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति ॥ २.१००.१९॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinmantrayase naika: kaccinna bahubhi: saha ।kaccitte mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṁ na paridhāvati ॥ 2.100.19॥

translations.english: O Bharata, having determined on an endeavour involving a little effort and yielding great results, I trust you commence to execute it quickly without procrastination?

verses.sloka: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम् ।क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्त्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव ॥ २.१००.२०॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidarthaṁ viniścitya laghumūlaṁ mahodayam ।kṣipramārabhase karttuṁ na dīrghayasi rāghava ॥ 2.100.20॥

translations.english: I trust, other kings come to know of your endeavours only when your endeavours suceed or about to succeed. I hope, efforts intended to be made in future are not revealed to them beforehand.
translations.hindi: अत्र हे वीर ! हम दोनों धनुष बाण ले इस पवत पर चढ़ चलें अथवा दोनों जन, कवच पाहून और हथियार णे यहीं खड़े हो जांय

verses.sloka: कच्चित्ते सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुन: ।विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्त्तव्यानि पार्थिवा: ॥ २.१००.२१॥
verses.transliteration: kaccitte sukṛtānyeva kṛtarūpāṇi vā puna: ।viduste sarvakāryāṇi na karttavyāni pārthivā: ॥ 2.100.21॥

translations.english: Dear brother, I hope others are not able to understand your determination or those of your ministers, either by conjecture or by inference or through other means without being revealed either by you or by your ministers.
translations.hindi: कोविदार ध्वजा वाले भरत को निश्चय ही हम लोग युद्ध में अपने वश में कर लेंगे । भरत केकारण ही तो यह विपत्ति आई हे । आज हम उसे समझ लेंगे

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्न तर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिता: ।त्वया वा वा ऽमात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम् ॥ २.१००.२२॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinna tarkairyuktyā vā ye cāpyaparikīrtitā: ।tvayā vā vā 'mātyairbudhyate tāta mantritam ॥ 2.100.22॥

translations.english: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.
translations.hindi: हे रघुनन्दन ! जिसके लिए तुम्हें, मुझे और सीता को इस ` दुदशा में पड़ना पड़ा है ओर जितके कारण तुम सनातन राज्य च्युत किए गए हो

verses.sloka: कच्चित् सहस्रान् मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम् ।पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्य्यान्नि:श्रेयसं महत् ॥ २.१००.२३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit sahasrān mūrkhāṇāmekamicchasi paṇḍitam ।paṇḍito hyarthakṛcchreṣu kuryyānni:śreyasaṁ mahat ॥ 2.100.23॥

translations.english: Even if the king seeks the assistance from thousands or tens of thousands of fools, they cannot render any help to him.

verses.sloka: सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां यद्युपास्ते महीपति: ।अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता ॥ २.१००.२४॥
verses.transliteration: sahasrāṇyapi mūrkhāṇāṁ yadyupāste mahīpati: ।athavāpyayutānyeva nāsti teṣu sahāyatā ॥ 2.100.24॥

translations.english: A single clearsighted minister who is prudent, brave and skilful can bring about great prosperity to a king or a prince.
translations.hindi: क्योंकि पूव अपकारी को मार. डालने में कुछ भी पाप नहीं लगता । हे राबव ! यह भरत पूर्व में अपकार कर चुका है । अतः इसको मार डालने ही में पुण्य है

verses.sloka: एकोप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षण: ।राजानं राजमात्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम् ॥ २.१००.२५॥
verses.transliteration: ekopyamātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇa: ।rājānaṁ rājamātraṁ vā prāpayenmahatīṁ śriyam ॥ 2.100.25॥

translations.english: I hope you have employed highly competent servants for important tasks, mediocre servants in mediocre tasks and low people in inferior tasks.
translations.hindi: इसको मार कर आप सम्पूण प्रथिवी के राज्य का उप- भोग कीजिए । आज वह केकेयी जो राज्य पाने की कामना किए हुए है अपने पुत्र को युद्ध में मरा हुआ दखेगी

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्मुख्या महत्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमा: ।जघन्यास्तु जघन्येषु भृत्या: कर्मसु योजिता: ॥ २.१००.२६॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinmukhyā mahatsveva madhyameṣu ca madhyamā: ।jaghanyāstu jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyā: karmasu yojitā: ॥ 2.100.26॥

translations.english: I hope you are assigning ministers, who are unyielding to bribery and other temptations, holding positions hereditarily and who are full of integrity and eminence, with superior tasks.
translations.hindi: हाथी के तोड़े हुए वृक्ष की तरह मेरे हाथ से भरत को मरा हुआ दुख, केकेयी अत्यन्त दुःखित होगी । मैं उस केकेयो को भी उसके भाबईन्दों और मंथरादि सहित मार डाल गा

verses.sloka: अमात्यानुपधातीतान् पितृपैतामहाञ्छुचीन् ।श्रेष्ठान् श्रेष्ठेषु कच्चित्त्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु ॥ २.१००.२७॥
verses.transliteration: amātyānupadhātītān pitṛpaitāmahāñchucīn ।śreṣṭhān śreṣṭheṣu kaccittvaṁ niyojayasi karmasu ॥ 2.100.27॥

translations.english: Are not the citizens of your kingdom agitated at severe punishment meted out to them reproaching your ministers?
translations.hindi: जिससे कि यह प्रथिवी उस केकेयी रूपी महापाप से छुट- कारा पा ज्ञाय । ह मान के देने वाले ! आज बहुत दिनों के रोके हुए क्रोध को और कैकेयी के किए हुए तिरस्कार को

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजितप्रजम् ।राष्ट्रं तवानुजानन्ति मन्त्रिण: कैकयीसुत ॥ २.१००.२८॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinnogreṇa daṇḍena bhṛśamudvejitaprajam ।rāṣṭraṁ tavānujānanti mantriṇa: kaikayīsuta ॥ 2.100.28॥

translations.english: Just like a performer of sacrifice scorns at an outcaste or a woman scorns at a lustful lover, do the subjects not scorn you for collecting taxes more than what is due?
translations.hindi: शत्र की सेना के ऊपर वैसे ही छोडूंगा जैसे सुखे णो के डेर पर आग छोड़ी जाती है। आज ही सैं चित्रकूट के बन को अपने तीखे बाणां से

verses.sloka: कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजका: पतितं यथा ।उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रिय: ॥ २.१००.२९॥
verses.transliteration: kaccittvāṁ nāvajānanti yājakā: patitaṁ yathā ।ugrapratigrahītāraṁ kāmayānamiva striya: ॥ 2.100.29॥

translations.english: A learned person but skilled in contrivances, a warrior with passion for wealth and a man ever engaged in corrupting the minds of servants must be slain. A king who does not kill them is himself killed in due course.

verses.sloka: उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसन्दूषणे रतम् ।शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स वध्यते ॥ २.१००.३०॥
verses.transliteration: upāyakuśalaṁ vaidyaṁ bhṛtyasandūṣaṇe ratam ।śūramaiśvaryakāmaṁ ca yo na hanti sa vadhyate ॥ 2.100.30॥

translations.english: I trust you have appointed a man who is cheerful, brave, sagacious, steadfast, honest, of a good family, loyal and efficient as the army chief.
translations.hindi: इति षण्णवतितमः सगः ॥ भ्राज सैं इस महासंग्राम में सेनासहित भरत का बध कर अपने धनुष और बाणों के ऋण से निस्सन्देंह उऋण हो जाऊगा

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च मतिमान् धृतिमाञ्छुचि: ।कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्ष: सेनापति: कृत: ॥ २.१००.३१॥
verses.transliteration: kacciddhṛṣṭaśca śūraśca matimān dhṛtimāñchuci: ।kulīnaścānuraktaśca dakṣa: senāpati: kṛta: ॥ 2.100.31॥

translations.english: I trust you honour and respect those prominent soldiers who are courageous, powerful, skilled in war and who have proven heroic exploits.

verses.sloka: बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युद्धविशारदा: ।दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्य मानिता: ॥ २.१००.३२॥
verses.transliteration: balavantaśca kaccitte mukhyā yuddhaviśāradā: ।dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntāstvayā satkṛtya mānitā: ॥ 2.100.32॥

translations.english: I trust you distribute rations and wages to your army in due time without making delay.

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम् ।सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे ॥ २.१००.३३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidbalasya bhaktaṁ ca vetanaṁ ca yathocitam ।samprāptakālaṁ dātavyaṁ dadāsi na vilambase ॥ 2.100.33॥

translations.english: It has been mentioned in the scriptures that if provisions and wages are not paid in stipulated time, the dependent attendants will be incensed with their masters and will turn hostile and become corrupt, leading to great calamity.

verses.sloka: कालातिक्रमणाच्चैव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृता: ।भर्त्तु: कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सो ऽनर्थ: सुमहान् स्मृत: ॥ २.१००.३४॥
verses.transliteration: kālātikramaṇāccaiva bhaktavetanayorbhṛtā: ।bharttu: kupyanti duṣyanti so 'nartha: sumahān smṛta: ॥ 2.100.34॥

translations.english: I hope all men of a good family, especially those who belong to our race, are loyal to you and are ready to sacrifice their lives for your cause.

verses.sloka: कच्चित् सर्वे ऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्रा: प्रधानत: ।कच्चित्प्राणांस्तवार्थेषु सन्त्यजन्ति समाहिता: ॥ २.१००.३५॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit sarve 'nuraktāstvāṁ kulaputrā: pradhānata: ।kaccitprāṇāṁstavārtheṣu santyajanti samāhitā: ॥ 2.100.35॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I hope you have chosen as your envoy an expert born in your own country, wellinformed, skilful and quick to understand one who repeats and reports (exactly) what has been told.

verses.sloka: कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान् दक्षिण: प्रतिभानवान् ।यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डित: ॥ २.१००.३६॥
verses.transliteration: kaccijjānapado vidvān dakṣiṇa: pratibhānavān ।yathoktavādī dūtaste kṛto bharata paṇḍita: ॥ 2.100.36॥

translations.english: I hope you collect information (of their secret efforts) intelligently through unrecognisable spies with three of them closely watching each of the eighteen officials (there are eighteen categories of officials in a kingdom) of the enemy's side and fifteen (officials) on your side.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च ।त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकै: ॥ २.१००.३७॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidaṣṭādaśānyeṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca ।tribhistribhiravijñātairvetsi tīrthāni cārakai: ॥ 2.100.37॥

translations.english: O slayer of foes, I hope you are always alert about your foes who were defeated by you and have come back. You should not ignore your enemies thinking they are weak.

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान् प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा ।दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्त्तसे रिपुसूदन ॥ २.१००.३८॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidvyapāstānahitān pratiyātāṁśca sarvadā ।durbalānanavajñāya varttase ripusūdana ॥ 2.100.38॥

translations.english: Dear brother, I hope you do not serve those brahmins who are atheists, who foolishly think of this world alone and fancy themselves as learned. They only bring disasters.

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्न लोकायतिकान् ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे ।अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बाला: पण्डितमानिन: ॥ २.१००.३९॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinna lokāyatikān brāhmaṇāṁstāta sevase ।anarthakuśalā hyete bālā: paṇḍitamānina: ॥ 2.100.39॥

translations.english: While principal scriptures do exist, these superficial fellows take resort to the science of logic based on abstract reasoning, and indulge in futile talks.

verses.sloka: धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधा: ।बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते ॥ २.१००.४०॥
verses.transliteration: dharmaśāstreṣu mukhyeṣu vidyamāneṣu durbudhā: ।buddhimānvīkṣikīṁ prāpya nirarthaṁ pravadanti te ॥ 2.100.40॥

translations.english: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

verses.sloka: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकै: ।सत्यनामां दृढद्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम् ॥ २.१००.४१॥
verses.transliteration: vīrairadhyuṣitāṁ pūrvamasmākaṁ tāta pūrvakai: ।satyanāmāṁ dṛḍhadvārāṁ hastyaśvarathasaṅkulām ॥ 2.100.41॥

translations.english: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

verses.sloka: ब्राह्मणै: क्षत्ऺित्रयैर्वैश्यै: स्वकर्मनिरतै: सदा ।जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै: सहस्रश: ॥ २.१००.४२॥
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇai: kṣatऺitrayairvaiśyai: svakarmaniratai: sadā ।jitendriyairmahotsāhairvṛtāmāryai: sahasraśa: ॥ 2.100.42॥

translations.english: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

verses.sloka: प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम् ।कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि ॥ २.१००.४३॥
verses.transliteration: prāsādairvividhākārairvṛtāṁ vaidyajanākulām ।kaccitsumuditāṁ sphītāmayodhyāṁ parirakṣasi ॥ 2.100.43॥

translations.english: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

verses.sloka: कच्चिच्चित्यशतैर्जुष्ट: सुनिविष्टजनाकुल: ।देवस्थानै: प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभित: ॥ २.१००.४४॥
verses.transliteration: kacciccityaśatairjuṣṭa: suniviṣṭajanākula: ।devasthānai: prapābhiśca taṭākaiścopaśobhita: ॥ 2.100.44॥

translations.english: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

verses.sloka: प्रहृष्टनरनारीक: समाजोत्सवशोभित: ।सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान् हिंसाभि: परिवर्जित: ॥ २.१००.४५॥
verses.transliteration: prahṛṣṭanaranārīka: samājotsavaśobhita: ।sukṛṣṭasīmā paśumān hiṁsābhi: parivarjita: ॥ 2.100.45॥

translations.english: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

verses.sloka: अदेवमातृको रम्य: श्वापदै: परिवर्जित: ।परित्यक्तो भयै: सर्वै: खनिभिश्चोपशोभित: ॥ २.१००.४६॥
verses.transliteration: adevamātṛko ramya: śvāpadai: parivarjita: ।parityakto bhayai: sarvai: khanibhiścopaśobhita: ॥ 2.100.46॥

translations.english: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

verses.sloka: विवर्जितो नरै: पापैर्मम पूर्वै: सुरक्षित: ।कच्चिज्जनपद: स्फीत: सुखं वसति राघव ॥ २.१००.४७॥
verses.transliteration: vivarjito narai: pāpairmama pūrvai: surakṣita: ।kaccijjanapada: sphīta: sukhaṁ vasati rāghava ॥ 2.100.47॥

translations.english: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

verses.sloka: कच्चित्ते दयिता: सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविन: ।वार्त्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते ॥ २.१००.४८॥
verses.transliteration: kaccitte dayitā: sarve kṛṣigorakṣajīvina: ।vārttāyāṁ saṁśritastāta loko hi sukhamedhate ॥ 2.100.48॥

translations.english: I trust you nourish them and also afford portection and prevent adversities. A king must protect all those people living in his country in accordanc with righteousness.

verses.sloka: तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारै: कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम् ।रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिन: ॥ २.१००.४९॥
verses.transliteration: teṣāṁ guptiparīhārai: kaccitte bharaṇaṁ kṛtam ।rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsina: ॥ 2.100.49॥

translations.english: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

verses.sloka: कच्चित् स्त्रिय: सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिता: ।कच्चिन्न श्रद्दधास्यासां कच्चिद् गुह्यं न भाषसे ॥ २.१००.५०॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit striya: sāntvayasi kaccittāśca surakṣitā: ।kaccinna śraddadhāsyāsāṁ kaccid guhyaṁ na bhāṣase ॥ 2.100.50॥

translations.english: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुका: ।कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि ॥ २.१००.५१॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinnāgavanaṁ guptaṁ kaccitte santi dhenukā: ।kaccinna gaṇikāśvānāṁ kuñjarāṇāṁ ca tṛpyasi ॥ 2.100.51॥

translations.english: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम् ।उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे ॥ २.१००.५२॥
verses.transliteration: kacciddarśayase nityaṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ vibhūṣitam ।utthāyotthāya pūrvāhṇe rājaputra mahāpathe ॥ 2.100.52॥

translations.english: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

verses.sloka: कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ता: प्रत्यक्षास्ते ऽविशङ्कया ।सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम् ॥ २.१००.५३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccinna sarve karmāntā: pratyakṣāste 'viśaṅkayā ।sarve vā punarutsṛṣṭā madhyamevātra kāraṇam ॥ 2.100.53॥

translations.english: Hope all the forts are adequately provided with wealth, foodgrains, weapons and water, with machines of war and craftsmen and archers.

verses.sloka: कच्चित् सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकै: ।यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्द्धरै ॥ २.१००.५४॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit sarvāṇi durgāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakai: ।yantraiśca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurddharai ॥ 2.100.54॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I trust, your revenues are abundant and expenditure much less. I trust you do not give away your treasure to undeserving persons.

verses.sloka: आयस्ते विपुल: कच्चित् कच्चिदल्पतरो व्यय: ।अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव ॥ २.१००.५५॥
verses.transliteration: āyaste vipula: kaccit kaccidalpataro vyaya: ।apātreṣu na te kaccitkośo gacchati rāghava ॥ 2.100.55॥

translations.english: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

verses.sloka: देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थे ब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च ।योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्यय: ॥ २.१००.५६॥
verses.transliteration: devatārthe ca pitrarthe brāhmaṇābhyāgateṣu ca ।yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccidgacchati te vyaya: ॥ 2.100.56॥

translations.english: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदार्य्यो विशुद्धात्मा ऽ ऽक्षारितश्चोरकर्मणा ।अपृष्ट: शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचि: ॥ २.१००.५७॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidāryyo viśuddhātmā ' 'kṣāritaścorakarmaṇā ।apṛṣṭa: śāstrakuśalairna lobhādvadhyate śuci: ॥ 2.100.57॥

translations.english: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

verses.sloka: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्ट: सकारण: ।कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ ॥ २.१००.५८॥
verses.transliteration: gṛhītaścaiva pṛṣṭaśca kāle dṛṣṭa: sakāraṇa: ।kaccinna mucyate coro dhanalobhānnararṣabha ॥ 2.100.58॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

verses.sloka: व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव ।अर्थं विरागा: पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुता: ॥ २.१००.५९॥
verses.transliteration: vyasane kaccidāḍhyasya durgatasya ca rāghava ।arthaṁ virāgā: paśyanti tavāmātyā bahuśrutā: ॥ 2.100.59॥

translations.english: O Bharata, the tears falling from the eyes of persons, who are falsely accused and punished for the pleasure of the king will destroy his progeny and cattle as well.

verses.sloka: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यस्राणि राघव ।तानि पुत्रपशून् घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासत: ॥ २.१००.६०॥
verses.transliteration: yāni mithyābhiśastānāṁ patantyasrāṇi rāghava ।tāni putrapaśūn ghnanti prītyarthamanuśāsata: ॥ 2.100.60॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I trust you wish to thrive by treating the old, children and foremost of learned people with the three expedients namely gifts, affection and kind words.

verses.sloka: कच्चिद् वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यमुख्यांश्च राघव ।दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे ॥ २.१००.६१॥
verses.transliteration: kaccid vṛddhāṁśca bālāṁśca vaidyamukhyāṁśca rāghava ।dānena manasā vācā tribhiretairbubhūṣase ॥ 2.100.61॥

translations.english: I trust you pay homage to the preceptors, the aged ones, ascetics, gods and guests, to shrines and to accomplished brahmins.

verses.sloka: कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन् ।चैत्यांश्च सर्वान् सिद्धार्थान् ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि ॥ २.१००.६२॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidgurūṁśca vṛddhāṁśca tāpasān devatātithīn ।caityāṁśca sarvān siddhārthān brāhmaṇāṁśca namasyasi ॥ 2.100.62॥

translations.english: I trust, righteousness for the sake of prosperity or prosperity for the sake of righteousness or both for the sake of sensual pleasure are not thwarted by you.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुन: ।उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे ॥ २.१००.६३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidarthena vā dharmamarthaṁ dharmeṇa vā puna: ।ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena ca na bādhase ॥ 2.100.63॥

translations.english: O Bharata, the best among the victorious, conversant with timely actions and a bestower of boons you are the best of men. I trust, you allocate adequate time for attending to all the three expedients of life like dharma, artha and kama.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर ।विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान् वरद सेवसे ॥ २.१००.६४॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidarthaṁ ca dharmaṁ ca kāmaṁ ca jayatāṁ vara ।vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvān varada sevase ॥ 2.100.64॥

translations.english: O highly sagacious Bharata, those brahmins who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures along with the inhabitants of the city and country, I trust, are seeking your happiness.

verses.sloka: कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणा: शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदा: ।आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदै: सह ॥ २.१००.६५॥
verses.transliteration: kaccitte brāhmaṇā: śarma sarvaśāstrārthakovidā: ।āśaṁsante mahāprājña paurajānapadai: saha ॥ 2.100.65॥

translations.english: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

verses.sloka: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम् ।अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम् ॥ २.१००.६६॥
verses.transliteration: nāstikyamanṛtaṁ krodhaṁ pramādaṁ dīrghasūtratām ।adarśanaṁ jñānavatāmālasyaṁ pañcavṛttitām ॥ 2.100.66॥

translations.english: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

verses.sloka: एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम् ।निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम् ॥ २.१००.६७॥
verses.transliteration: ekacintanamarthānāmanarthajñaiśca mantraṇam ।niścitānāmanārambhaṁ mantrasyāparirakṣaṇam ॥ 2.100.67॥

translations.english: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

verses.sloka: मङ्गलस्याप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वत: ।कच्चित्त्वं वर्जयस्येतान् राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश ॥ २.१००.६८॥
verses.transliteration: maṅgalasyāprayogaṁ ca pratyutthānaṁ ca sarvata: ।kaccittvaṁ varjayasyetān rājadoṣāṁścaturdaśa ॥ 2.100.68॥

translations.english: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

verses.sloka: दश पञ्च चतुर्वर्गान् सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वत: ।अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव ॥ २.१००.६९॥
verses.transliteration: daśa pañca caturvargān saptavargaṁ ca tattvata: ।aṣṭavargaṁ trivargaṁ ca vidyāstisraśca rāghava ॥ 2.100.69॥

translations.english: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

verses.sloka: इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्वा षाङ्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम् ।कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गञ्च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम् ॥ २.१००.७०॥
verses.transliteration: indriyāṇāṁ jayaṁ buddhvā ṣāṅguṇyaṁ daivamānuṣam ।kṛtyaṁ viṁśativargañca tathā prakṛtimaṇḍalam ॥ 2.100.70॥

translations.english: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

verses.sloka: यात्रादण्डविधानञ्च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ ।कच्चिदेतान् महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे ॥ २.१००.७१॥
verses.transliteration: yātrādaṇḍavidhānañca dviyonī sandhivigrahau ।kaccidetān mahāprājña yathāvadanumanyase ॥ 2.100.71॥

translations.english: I trust you deliberate in secrecy on your counsel with three or four counsellors, together and separately with each one, as laid down in sacred texts.

verses.sloka: मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टैश्चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा ।कच्चित् समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्र मन्त्रयसे मिथ: ॥ २.१००.७२॥
verses.transliteration: mantribhistvaṁ yathoddiṣṭaiścaturbhistribhireva vā ।kaccit samastairvyastaiśca mantra mantrayase mitha: ॥ 2.100.72॥

translations.english: I trust, the Vedas you have studied are fruitful, the acts which you commenced are productive, your wife is fruitful (blessed with a son) and the scriptures you studied are useful.

verses.sloka: कच्चित्ते सफला वेदा: कच्चित्ते सफला: क्रिया: ।कच्चित्ते सफला दारा: कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम् ॥ २.१००.७३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccitte saphalā vedā: kaccitte saphalā: kriyā: ।kaccitte saphalā dārā: kaccitte saphalaṁ śrutam ॥ 2.100.73॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I trust your intellect is in conformity with what I said conducive to long life, and fame in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity.

verses.sloka: कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव ।आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थसंहिता ॥ २.१००.७४॥
verses.transliteration: kaccideṣaiva te buddhiryathoktā mama rāghava ।āyuṣyā ca yaśasyā ca dharmakāmārthasaṁhitā ॥ 2.100.74॥

translations.english: I trust, you walk the auspicious path of truth (virtue) followed by our father and forefathers.

verses.sloka: यां वृत्तिं वर्त्तते तातो यां च न: प्रपितामहा: ।तां वृत्तिं वर्त्तसे कच्चिद्या च सत्पथगा शुभा ॥ २.१००.७५॥
verses.transliteration: yāṁ vṛttiṁ varttate tāto yāṁ ca na: prapitāmahā: ।tāṁ vṛttiṁ varttase kaccidyā ca satpathagā śubhā ॥ 2.100.75॥

translations.english: O Bharata, I trust you do not partake delicious food all by yourself, and you share it with your friends when they want it.

verses.sloka: कच्चित् स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव ।कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्य: सम्प्रयच्छसि ॥ २.१००.७६॥
verses.transliteration: kaccit svādu kṛtaṁ bhojyameko nāśnāsi rāghava ।kaccidāśaṁsamānebhyo mitrebhya: samprayacchasi ॥ 2.100.76॥

translations.english: The highly sagacious and learned king, having acquired the entire earth and punishing the people in accordance with tradition and righteously ruling the kingdom, will ascend the his release (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे शततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

verses.sloka: राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा महामतिर्दण्डधर: प्रजानाम् ।अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथावदितश्च्युत: स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान् ॥ २.१००.७७ ॥
verses.transliteration: rājā tu dharmeṇa hi pālayitvā mahāmatirdaṇḍadhara: prajānām ।avāpya kṛtsnāṁ vasudhāṁ yathāvaditaścyuta: svargamupaiti vidvān ॥ 2.100.77 ॥
